ds: Laundering of funds from ransomware, business email compromise, investment and romance scams, hacking and account takeover. Money mules, rapid cross-border transfers, crypto conversion and cash-out services are typical.

src.t: FATF, Illicit Financial Flows from Cyber-Enabled Fraud (2023)
FATF, Updated Guidance for a Risk-Based Approach to Virtual Assets and Virtual Asset Service Providers (2021)
Europol, Internet Organised Crime Threat Assessment (IOCTA) (annual; specify year)

cn.rt: Cybercrime proceeds, ATO, scams and mule cash-out on retail accounts, card fraud and loan fraud, via digital and phone social engineering.

rat: Scam, BEC and ransomware proceeds via mules, instant payments and crypto.

ind.n: New account receives funds from many victims then moves them out
ind.cx: Incoming payments from unrelated individuals followed by transfers abroad or to crypto.
ind.ds: A new or low-activity account receives payments from several unrelated individuals who appear to be victims of fraud or phishing, followed by onward movement or cash-out.
ind.cn: Account receiving funds from multiple apparent fraud victims

ind.n: Payment-instruction changes and urgent transfers to new beneficiaries
ind.ds: Staff receive urgent, confidential requests, or changes to beneficiary details, directing payment to a new beneficiary outside normal workflow.
ind.cn: Urgent payment instruction or payment-detail change outside normal process

ind.n: Customers sending funds to crypto exchanges after being contacted by 'advisers'

ind.cx: Payments to wallets attributed to ransomware.
ind.ds: Customer transacts directly or near-directly with blockchain addresses attributed by sanctions lists or analytics to designated persons, thefts, ransomware or terrorist fundraising.
ind.cn: Exposure to wallets attributed to designated, stolen-fund or illicit actors

ind.n: Account takeover indicators with immediate credential change and large outflows
ind.ds: Password, email or phone details are changed, followed in the same session or day by a new payee and large outbound payments.
ind.cn: Credential or contact change followed by new payee and payments

ind.n: Rapid chain-hopping, mixers and privacy coin conversion
ind.cx: Funds move across tokens and chains.
ind.ds: Funds are moved through mixers, privacy coins or rapid cross-chain conversion to obscure origin.
ind.cn: Use of mixers, chain-hopping or privacy coins

ind.n: Accounts opened with synthetic or stolen identities
ind.ds: Identity documents, contact details, geolocation or device data do not align, suggesting fabricated, stolen or misrepresented identity.
ind.cn: Inconsistent or synthetic identity data at onboarding

ind.n: Cash-out through gift cards, prepaid, or money mules in other countries

ctl.ds: Places risk-based holds on uncleared or unusual inbound items and funds, limiting withdrawal until the item is confirmed good. It protects against losses from counterfeit, reversible or suspicious deposits.
Model that scores inbound-then-outbound pass-through, new-payee churn, counterparty diversity and profile mismatch to flag likely mule accounts. It prioritises accounts for review and restriction.
Verifies instructions, detail changes and unusual requests by contacting the customer on a channel held on file, never one supplied in the request. It defeats impersonation and account takeover.
Rules that alert on abnormal count, value or speed of movements over defined windows compared with customer profile and peer norms. They provide baseline coverage across many typologies.

ctl.n: Dynamic payment friction and scam warnings
ctl.ds: Risk-scored payments trigger a purpose question and a tailored scam warning, or a call-back, before release to the customer. It gives the customer a chance to reconsider and interrupts payments made under deception.

Trains branch, contact-centre and relationship staff to ask open questions, recognise coaching, coercion, pressure and evasion and escalate with authority to pause. It strengthens the human control at the point of contact.
Traces exposure of deposit and withdrawal addresses to illicit clusters and screens wallets with risk-scored alerts. It reveals on-chain exposure.

Routes potential sanctions, proscription or restricted-party exposure to a specialist sanctions or legal team for decision before proceeding, and sets conditions for finance and insurance. It ensures complex legal judgements are made by qualified people.
Analyses typing, navigation, remote-access tooling, call-in-progress signals and deviation from baseline to spot coached, scripted or hijacked sessions. It detects coercion and takeover.
Requires phishing-resistant authentication and additional verification on risky sessions, credential or payee changes and large payments. It blocks unauthorised access and payments.

ctl.n: Counterparty VASP and platform due diligence
ctl.ds: Assesses the licensing, AML controls, jurisdiction and reputation of counterparty exchanges, over-the-counter desks and other virtual asset service providers before enabling flows, and reviews them periodically. It limits exposure through weak or complicit counterparties.

Fingerprints devices, IP addresses, emulators and network attributes to link applications, sessions and accounts and to flag shared or anomalous infrastructure. It exposes mule rings and multiple-account abuse.

Remote verification of a person's identity using document capture, biometric matching and liveness or anti-spoofing checks, or a trusted digital identity. It reduces impersonation, synthetic identities and account opening with stolen or fabricated credentials.

Provides targeted messaging that helps customers recognise scam scripts and mule recruitment, verify requests independently and use trusted routes for giving or paying. It reduces victimisation and unwitting participation.

Translates published and sanitised typologies and red flags into targeted monitoring scenarios and context-aware rules that are reviewed periodically. It aligns monitoring with known criminal methods.
